title: Token-trajectory bucketing and pad-minimizer: adaptive micro-batch shaping
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current micro-batch shapers use coarse-length buckets that still leave >10% wasted compute on common chat workloads due to right-padding. This increases per-token cost and occasionally pushes latency SLOs for short, latency-sensitive requests. The goal of this ticket is to design and implement an adaptive bucketer that assigns requests based on observed "token trajectory" (their expected prefill + decode length distribution) and to couple that with a pad-minimizer that heuristically trims and coalesces paddings without violating kernel-alignment constraints or increasing KV-cache churn.
background: Existing work has reduced padding via static bucketing and prefill-aware coalescing, but we see tail cases where sequences diverge during decode (streaming chat with user edits, followed by long system messages). Kernel selection is sensitive to stride and contiguous memory shapes; naive trimming can force slower kernels. We need an approach that balances pad reduction with kernel affinity and causal attention scheduling.
proposed_solution:
1) Introduce a lightweight per-request token-trajectory sketch (three-number summary: observed_prefill_len, expected_decode_mean, decode_variance) computed at enqueue time.
2) Use a dynamic bucketing policy that groups requests by trajectory vicinity instead of absolute max length. Buckets adapt every N seconds based on recent traffic histograms.
3) Implement a pad-minimizer step pre-kernel that: a) performs suffix-trim when decode_variance is low, b) applies micro-suffix-merge for requests whose trailing pads are contiguous in memory, and c) preserves alignment constraints required by fast kernels (e.g., block-32 alignment).
4) Extend kernel-affinity scorer to consider adjusted shapes post-trim; prefer kernels that maximize throughput for fused bucket shapes.
5) Add a fallback mechanism: if a trimmed request causes >5% KV cache misses on decode, automatically revert trimming for that request class for 10 minutes.
design_notes:
- Trajectory sketch must be cheap: avoid storing large histograms per request. Use exponentially-weighted moving averages at the route level to seed expected_decode_mean.
- Buckets are defined in a 2D space (prefill_len, expected_decode_mean) with clustering via incremental k-means (k bounded, latency budget aware).
- Pad-minimizer must integrate with current prefill coalescer. Implement as a separate pass to keep modifications minimal.
- Kernel-affinity scoreboard will rank candidates by expected p50 latency and gpu_util for the shaped batch. Scores persisted for 1 minute to avoid oscillation.
- Instrumentation: expose per-bucket wasted-pad tokens, p50/p95 latency, kernel chosen, and KV cache miss rate.
tradeoffs:
- Aggressive trimming reduces wasted compute but can increase KV-cache misses and require slow kernels if shapes become irregular.
- More buckets reduce padding but increase scheduling complexity and potentially lower batch occupancy.
- Trajectory sketches add bookkeeping overhead but should be amortized across requests; must be bounded in memory.
- Incremental clustering yields non-deterministic bucket boundaries; we'll mitigate with seed stabilization and hysteresis.
milestones: M1: Prototype token-trajectory sketch and offline simulation (week 1)
M2: Implement dynamic bucketer + pad-minimizer in runtime (week 2)
M3: Integrate kernel-affinity scorer and safe fallback (week 3)
M4: Canary rollout to low-traffic region + monitoring dashboards (week 4)
rollout_plan: Canary to 2% of traffic routed through a dedicated pool. Monitor: wasted-pad-tokens, p50/p95 latency, per-request cost. If any of these regress beyond predefined thresholds (p95 latency +10% or wasted-pad reduction <5%), pause rollout and revert. Gradually increase to 25% then 100% over two weeks if stable.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for sketch update and bucketing logic.
- End-to-end benchmark harness using replayed production traces with label-preserving shuffles.
- GPU microbenchmarks verifying kernel selection stability across shaped batches.
- Chaos test: inject variable decode variance to ensure fallback triggers correctly.
- A/B experiment comparing cost-per-token and latency against current shaper for 1M requests.
metrics: p50_latency_ms / p95_latency_ms (no more than +5% p95 during canary)
blockers: Need small-alloc GPU buffer API to do in-place pad coalescing (infra ticket)
Precise kernel alignment constraints not documented for some vendor kernels; awaiting input from HW team
